## Current Projects

### Network-aware random forests for correlated, high-dimensional data
*With Dr. Christina Ramirez, UCLA Biostatistics*

Developing **mossyforest**, an interpretable, network-aware, tree-based feature selection method for highly correlated data using SHAP values, Recursive Feature Elimination, and stability selection. Currently we are extending it to longitudinal data through time-aware network reduction and mixed-effects trees. Applied to 800,000+ CpG sites of DNA methylation to identify HIV-related epigenetic biomarkers of aging.

### Predicting Mental Health through Passive Sensing data
*With Dr. Brunilda Balliu, UCLA Computational Medicine*

Building machine learning and deep learning models that use passive wearable and smartphone sensing data to predict depression severity. Work includes deep learning imputation (autoencoders, self-attention transformers), predictive modeling, and subtyping of latent mental health states with multivariate hidden Markov models.

### Age and brain network structure in the Aging Adult Brain Connectome
*With Dr. Helen Lavretsky and Dr. Christina Ramirez, UCLA*

Applying network-guided machine learning to brain markers and biomarkers to model cognitive outcomes, and characterizing how age modifies correlation network structure and predictor importance.
